opening_message:
Ticket 1: Christopher Myers (employee ID E012) requests write access to Source Code.

Team memory: 2 note(s) about employee E012.
Note 1 (ticket 1), written by HR agent:
  - role: Analyst (looked up in own database before writing)
  - employment type: full_time (looked up in own database before writing)
  - recommendation for Source Code: write
  - comment: Employee is a full-time Analyst requesting write access to Source Code. Full-time employees may have up to write (admin only if their role owns the system; Analyst does not own Source Code). Requested level is write, which is within policy, so recommend write.
Note 2 (ticket 1), written by Security agent:
  - role: Analyst (not looked up in own database before writing; same value as note 1 by HR agent)
  - employment type: contractor (looked up in own database before writing)
  - security training: basic (looked up in own database before writing)
  - recommendation for Source Code: read
  - comment: Security DB shows E012 is a contractor with basic security training (HR note said full-time, but security records govern here). Contractors may have read, or write only with advanced training. Requested write exceeds max, so grant read.

Per policy, contractors may have read, or write only with advanced security training. Since the employee has basic training, the maximum allowed is read. content.text:
Let me analyze this ticket.

The employee Christopher Myers (E012) requests write access to Source Code.

There are two notes:
- HR note: role Analyst, employment type full_time, recommendation write.
- Security note: role Analyst (not looked up), employment type contractor (looked up), security training basic, recommendation read. Security note says security records govern.

Access policy:
1. full_time employees: up to write. Admin only if role owns system.
2. contractor employees: read, or write if advanced security training. Never admin.

Source Code is owned by Engineer role. Analyst does not own Source Code.

The conflict: HR says full_time, Security says contractor with basic training.

Which governs? The Security agent says "security records govern here." We have conflicting facts. Typically in these scenarios, the security agent's database is authoritative for employment type/security training. The notes themselves tell us: HR looked up employment type in own database, Security looked up employment type in own database and security training in own database. They conflict. The Security agent says security records govern.

So employee is contractor with basic training. Contractors: read, or write only with advanced training. Basic training → max is read. Requested write > max, so grant read.

Submit decision: read with evidence.

Let me do that.
